content:
# Adding us-west-2 Region to Crossplane Composition

To add a second AWS region (us-west-2) idiomatically in Crossplane without changing claims, follow this approach:

## 1. Create Regional ProviderConfigs

Define separate `ProviderConfig` resources for each region:

```yaml
---
# provider-config-us-east-1.yaml
apiVersion: aws.crossplane.io/v1beta1
kind: ProviderConfig
metadata:
  name: aws-us-east-1
  namespace: crossplane-system
spec:
  credentials:
    source: Secret
    secretRef:
      namespace: crossplane-system
      name: aws-creds
      key: creds
  region: us-east-1
---
# provider-config-us-west-2.yaml
apiVersion: aws.crossplane.io/v1beta1
kind: ProviderConfig
metadata:
  name: aws-us-west-2
  namespace: crossplane-system
spec:
  credentials:
    source: Secret
    secretRef:
      namespace: crossplane-system
      name: aws-creds
      key: creds
  region: us-west-2
```

## 2. Update the CompositeResourceDefinition (XRD)

Add an optional `region` parameter to the XRD spec, defaulting to `us-east-1` to remain backward-compatible with existing claims:

```yaml
apiVersion: apiextensions.crossplane.io/v1
kind: CompositeResourceDefinition
metadata:
  name: xapplications.example.com
spec:
  group: example.com
  names:
    kind: XApplication
  claimNames:
    kind: Application
  versions:
  - name: v1alpha1
    served: true
    referenceable: true
    schema:
      openAPIV3Schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          spec:
            type: object
            properties:
              region:
                type: string
                enum: ["us-east-1", "us-west-2"]
                default: "us-east-1"
                description: "AWS region for primary deployment"
              environment:
                type: string
                enum: ["dev", "prod"]
              # ... other parameters
            required: ["environment"]
```

## 3. Update the Composition

Patch resources to use the correct ProviderConfig based on the region parameter:

```yaml
apiVersion: apiextensions.crossplane.io/v1
kind: Composition
metadata:
  name: application.example.com
spec:
  compositeTypeRef:
    apiVersion: example.com/v1alpha1
    kind: XApplication
  resources:
  # EKS Cluster
  - name: eks-cluster
    base:
      apiVersion: eks.aws.crossplane.io/v1beta1
      kind: Cluster
      spec:
        forProvider:
          region: us-east-1  # Will be patched
          version: "1.27"
        providerConfigRef:
          name: aws-us-east-1  # Will be patched
    patches:
    - type: FromCompositeFieldValue
      fromFieldPath: spec.region
      toFieldPath: spec.forProvider.region
    - type: FromCompositeFieldValue
      fromFieldPath: spec.region
      toFieldPath: spec.providerConfigRef.name
      transforms:
      - type: string
        string:
          fmt: "aws-%s"
    connectionDetails:
    - fromConnectionDetailKey: kubeconfig
      name: kubeconfig
      type: SecretKey
  
  # S3 Bucket (primary region)
  - name: s3-bucket
    base:
      apiVersion: s3.aws.crossplane.io/v1beta1
      kind: Bucket
      spec:
        providerConfigRef:
          name: aws-us-east-1
    patches:
    - type: FromCompositeFieldValue
      fromFieldPath: spec.region
      toFieldPath: spec.providerConfigRef.name
      transforms:
      - type: string
        string:
          fmt: "aws-%s"
    - type: FromCompositeFieldValue
      fromFieldPath: metadata.name
      toFieldPath: metadata.name
      transforms:
      - type: string
        string:
          fmt: "%s-bucket"
    # Enable versioning and encryption
    - type: FromCompositeFieldValue
      fromFieldPath: spec.region
      toFieldPath: spec.forProvider.versioningConfiguration.status
      transforms:
      - type: string
        string:
          fmt: "Enabled"

  # RDS Instance
  - name: rds-instance
    base:
      apiVersion: rds.aws.crossplane.io/v1alpha1
      kind: DBInstance
      spec:
        providerConfigRef:
          name: aws-us-east-1
        forProvider:
          allocatedStorage: "20"
          engine: postgres
    patches:
    - type: FromCompositeFieldValue
      fromFieldPath: spec.region
      toFieldPath: spec.providerConfigRef.name
      transforms:
      - type: string
        string:
          fmt: "aws-%s"
    - type: FromCompositeFieldValue
      fromFieldPath: spec.environment
      toFieldPath: spec.forProvider.dbInstanceClass
      transforms:
      - type: map
        map:
          dev: "db.t3.micro"
          prod: "db.t3.medium"
    - type: FromCompositeFieldValue
      fromFieldPath: spec.environment
      toFieldPath: spec.forProvider.multiAZ
      transforms:
      - type: map
        map:
          dev: false
          prod: true

  # Managed Node Group
  - name: managed-node-group
    base:
      apiVersion: eks.aws.crossplane.io/v1alpha1
      kind: NodeGroup
      spec:
        providerConfigRef:
          name: aws-us-east-1
        forProvider:
          scalingConfig:
            desiredSize: 2
    patches:
    - type: FromCompositeFieldValue
      fromFieldPath: spec.region
      toFieldPath: spec.providerConfigRef.name
      transforms:
      - type: string
        string:
          fmt: "aws-%s"
    - type: FromCompositeFieldValue
      fromFieldPath: spec.environment
      toFieldPath: spec.forProvider.scalingConfig.desiredSize
      transforms:
      - type: map
        map:
          dev: 2
          prod: 4
```

## 4. Deploy and Test (Without Changing Existing Claims)

Existing claims remain unchanged:

```yaml
apiVersion: example.com/v1alpha1
kind: Application
metadata:
  name: myapp-dev
spec:
  environment: dev
  # region defaults to us-east-1 — backward compatible
```

Deploy new claims to us-west-2:

```yaml
apiVersion: example.com/v1alpha1
kind: Application
metadata:
  name: myapp-prod-west
spec:
  region: us-west-2
  environment: prod
```

## Key Points

- **Backward Compatibility**: Existing claims work unchanged (default to us-east-1)
- **Idiomatic Crossplane**: Region selection via ProviderConfig refs and composition patches
- **No Claim Changes**: The XRD is extended optionally; claims are independently deployable
- **Cross-Region Replication**: For prod S3, add a separate bucket resource or ReplicationConfiguration targeting the us-west-2 bucket as the replication destination
- **Multi-Region RDS**: Use `createDBInstanceReadReplica` to create a read replica in us-west-2 for prod, referencing the primary instance

This approach satisfies environment isolation—dev and prod can independently specify their regions via claims, and the composition patches resources to use the appropriate regional provider config.
